title: Rigveda 2.8: To Agni
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 2.8: To Agni: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 2.8 is a hymn of 6 verses addressed to Agni. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 2, the family book of Gṛtsamada. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 154v-155r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 2.8.2-6 (aṣṭaka 2, adhyāya 5, varga 29); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 155r
translation.original_text:
2yaḥ su̍nī̱tho da̍dā̱śuṣe̍ 'ju̱ryo ja̱raya̍nn a̱rim | cāru̍pratīka̱ āhu̍taḥ ||
3ya u̍ śri̱yā dame̱ṣv ā do̱ṣoṣasi̍ praśa̱syate̍ | yasya̍ vra̱taṁ na mīya̍te ||
4ā yaḥ sva1̱̍r ṇa bhā̱nunā̍ ci̱tro vi̱bhāty a̱rciṣā̍ | a̱ñjā̱no a̱jarai̍r a̱bhi ||
5atri̱m anu̍ sva̱rājya̍m a̱gnim u̱kthāni̍ vāvṛdhuḥ | viśvā̱ adhi̱ śriyo̍ dadhe ||
6a̱gner indra̍sya̱ soma̍sya de̱vānā̍m ū̱tibhi̍r va̱yam | ari̍ṣyantaḥ sacemahy a̱bhi ṣyā̍ma pṛtanya̱taḥ ||
translation.text:
2Who, guiding worshippers aright, withers, untouched by age, the foe: When worshipped fair to look upon;
3Who for his glory is extolled at eve and morning in our homes, Whose statute is inviolate;
4Who shines refulgent like the Sun, with brilliance and with fiery flame, Decked with imperishable sheen.
5Him Atri, Agni, have our songs Strengthened according to his sway: All glories hath he made his own.
6May we with Agni's, Indra's help, with Soma's, yea, of all the Gods, Uninjured dwell together still, and conquer those who fight with us.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 155r (numbered 1r by the scribe) (OPenn image 156, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 2.8.2 ‹cāru-pratīkaḥ āhutaḥ›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 155v (numbered 1v by the scribe), begins in RV 2.9.3 ‹yaje tam pra tve›. Verses 2.8.2-6 end on this page; 2.8.2 begins on fol. 154v (numbered 12v by the scribe).

3yaḥ | oṃ iti | śriyā | dameṣu | ā | doṣā | uṣasi | pra-śasyate | yasya | vratam | na | mīyate
4ā | yaḥ | svaḥ | na | bhānunā | citraḥ | vi-bhāti | arciṣā | añjānaḥ | ajaraiḥ | abhi
